subject: botany_2
question_text: What are the physiological processes that are regulated by ethylene in plants?

mark_split.label: Growth in water plants and roots

insider_note: Ethylene is the only gaseous hormone, and that is worth the first line. Fruit ripening is the effect an examiner will not accept an answer without.

steps.label: What ethylene is
steps.margin_note: Gas, source, and why the gas matters. Five lines.
lines: Ethylene is a simple GASEOUS plant growth
regulator.
It is produced in large amounts by ripening
fruits and by ageing tissues.
Because it is a gas, it spreads from one fruit
to the fruits around it.
steps.why: Being a gas is what lets one ripe fruit ripen a whole basket, which no liquid hormone could do.
common_mistakes: Calling ethylene a liquid hormone. It is a GAS, and that is its defining feature.
Saying it is made only in seeds. Ripening fruits and ageing tissues make the most.
steps.memory_tip: The only gas among the hormones, so it travels through the air.

steps.label: Ripening and senescence
steps.margin_note: Three numbered effects. Ripening and the respiratory climactic are the two to name.
lines: 1. Ethylene is highly effective in FRUIT
RIPENING.
2. It raises the rate of respiration during
ripening. This rise is called the RESPIRATORY
CLIMACTIC.
3. It promotes SENESCENCE and ABSCISSION of
leaves and flowers.
steps.why: Ripening is an active process that needs energy, so the burst of respiration is what pays for it — which is why the two always appear together.
common_mistakes: Saying ethylene delays ripening. It PROMOTES ripening.
Leaving out abscission. Ethylene causes leaves and flowers to fall.
steps.memory_tip: Ethylene ends things: ripens, ages, and drops.

steps.label: Seedling and dormancy effects
steps.margin_note: Three numbered effects. The hook is the one most often forgotten.
lines: 4. In dicot seedlings it causes horizontal
growth, swelling of the axis, and APICAL HOOK
formation.
5. It BREAKS seed and bud dormancy.
6. It starts germination in peanut seeds and
sprouting in potato tubers.
steps.why: The apical hook protects the shoot tip as the seedling pushes up through soil, so ethylene is what shapes a seedling to survive emergence.
common_mistakes: Saying ethylene causes dormancy. It BREAKS dormancy.
Leaving out the apical hook. It is the named seedling response.
steps.memory_tip: Hook, swell, and break dormancy: all of it happens underground.

steps.label: Growth in water plants and roots
steps.margin_note: Two more numbered effects. Eight in total is a full answer.

lines.text: Ethylene ripens, ages, drops and elongates

lines: 7. In water plants it promotes rapid PETIOLE
and INTERNODE elongation, so leaves stay above
rising water.
8. It promotes root growth and ROOT HAIR
formation, which increases absorption.
steps.why: A deep-water rice plant that cannot grow taller than the flood will drown, so ethylene-driven elongation is a survival response, not just a growth effect.
common_mistakes: Saying ethylene stops root growth. It PROMOTES root and root hair growth.
Leaving out the water plants. The elongation response is a named application.
steps.memory_tip: Rising water, rising stem: the leaves stay in the air.
